Container.Name: numa-home
Container.Overview:
Numa Home shows every photograph in the house in a browser, on a phone or on the TV. Raws such as RAF, ARW, CR3, NEF and DNG are rendered with Numa's colour and your edits. Faces are found and grouped, and search understands words such as "beach at sunset". An account for each person, albums, stars and picks shared by the household, Send Home from the Numa apps for Linux, Mac and iPhone, and import from an SD card in the server. One container with SQLite; nothing goes to the cloud.
Open the WebUI and make the first account: it is the admin. On the first start the face and search models (about 520 MB) are downloaded into /data, and then the photographs are read in the background. Numa Home writes a small catalog into a .numa folder inside each library, so the photographs share must be writable.
Container.Requires: An x86-64 (amd64) server. Internet access on the first start, to download the face and search models.

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: The web page and the apps' connection.

Config.Name: Photographs
Config.Description: Your photographs. Every library in it is shown; Numa Home keeps a small catalog in each library's .numa folder.

Config.Name: Sent Home
Config.Description: What each account sends home from the Numa apps.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Accounts, thumbnails, models and the nightly database copies.

Config.Name: Cards
Config.Description: Optional: where SD cards and USB drives are mounted, for example /mnt/disks, to import from the browser.

Config.Name: Second copy
Config.Description: Optional: a second disk; every night the photographs and the database copies are mirrored to it.

Config.Name: Reverse proxies
Config.Description: Only behind a reverse proxy: its address or network as Numa Home sees it, comma separated, for example 172.18.0.1. Without it the session cookie has no Secure, there is no HSTS and the sign-in limit counts every visitor as the proxy.

Config.Name: Intel or AMD GPU
Config.Description: Optional: /dev/dri for faster decoding. Everything works without it.
